assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only the subject's single curated item, reviewed-dedicated-analysis: the canonical V2 character reconstruction model MHA_SP2_TOGATA_MIRIO_CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MODEL.md at basis_commit, read in full as reviewed repository analysis of the Japanese main manga V01-V42 with the source-labeled Ultra Archive, Ultra Analysis and Ultra Age claims its TM-SUP-01 to TM-SUP-03 sections admit. The MHA character modeling schema was consulted for method only; the readiness index, supplemental reconciliation ledger and audit and the V14-V17 deep readings are not curated evidence on this subject and nothing is borrowed from them. The model's strong readiness label and its retrospective holdout probe are inputs, not conclusions. No original manga page, anime adaptation, V1 material or other character's model is included, and the evaluator performed no primary-source inspection.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: Togata Mirio from his V14 introduction as a Permeation-using third-year senior (V14:p071-115) through the V15-V17 Eri rescue and loss of Permeation (V17:p050-096), the V18 Quirkless grieving state (V18:p074-090), restoration after Eri's trained Rewind (V30:p138-140), the V36 restored professional in the final war (V36:p163-174) and the V42 graduation and adult No.1 epilogue (V42:p042-043, p149-152), kept as separable action spaces (with Permeation, Quirkless, restored, adult). No atom covers the V19-V29 Quirkless interval, and the supplement's agency succession and adult gag material are endpoint claims, not enacted scenes.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit; evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The model states a priority structure (rescue, a future where people can smile, reliable trained competence, sustaining those who made him capable), an ideal self (a dependable hero whose weakness was worked on, not hidden), a feared self (failing someone he could have protected), a non-ownership boundary (loss creates no entitlement to another person's capacity, TM04) and a default decision policy (define the reachable protective task, use practice, keep a forward social frame, help others act). Each rests on six located atoms TM01-TM06 across V14-V42 at high confidence. Not B: one compact secondary artifact with six atoms and one retrospective probe, and the model itself leaves independent adult and private breadth OPEN. Not D: the policy is operational and yields located conditional predictions with flip conditions.

Four action spaces are distinguished and located in story-present: Permeation-using senior (TM01-TM02), Quirkless grieving student (TM03-TM04, V17-V18), restored professional (TM05, V30 and V36) and adult No.1 (TM06, V42). The model states these are distinct action spaces, not cosmetic snapshots, and keeps grief and forward orientation coexisting. Not B: each transition is sampled by one atom, the V19-V29 interval has no atom, and the probe rates the emotional trajectory only partial because full adjustment is unseen. Not D: transitions are located over the whole series rather than sketched.

Attested features are few: 俺, bright direct address and playful reframing toward juniors, respectful senior-facing speech, the concise polite refusal いらないです (V18), the terminal plea to サー, and a brief sincere apology (V36). The probe's speech axis is supported on one refusal line. These answer bounded canon questions about register only; the model warns that humor should not fill every line, and the discovery row does not enroll SPEECH for this subject. Not D: no sampled range of ordinary, adult or private speech.

Ordinary texture is the comic recovery from a failed entrance (TM01), humor as a recurring social practice, and the supplement's adult peach-harvesting gag with differentiated child and elderly reception (TM-SUP-01) and agency sequence (TM-SUP-03). The model states that unrelated adult intimacy and family decision-making remain less certain and that repeated independent private and adult contexts are thinner.

A six-row partner table (Nighteye, Tamaki, Eri, Midoriya, Ochako and adult teams, an opponent with an unseen wound) gives a one-sentence conditional difference for each, and every row ties to a located atom (TM01-TM06), including the reciprocal Tamaki relation (TM02) and the misfired taunt and apology (TM05). Not C: per-partner deltas are sketched rather than worked, each partner rests on one or two scenes, and family and private relationships are absent.

Retrospective guilt after correct restraint (TM02), open grief and dependence on Nighteye (TM04) and the claim that confidence is practiced rather than effortless (TM01) are inferred from displayed behavior and speech. The model gives no internal monologue analysis and warns that his warmth does not imply perfect reading of others. Substantial inference without a demonstrated interior model.

Located conflict covers correct pursuit restraint (TM02), bodily defense of Eri after losing Permeation using trained prediction (TM03), a taunt that hits a real wound followed by apology and coordinated time-buying (TM05), and the policy that pressure can narrow the objective to preserving people and time. Not C: each mode rests on one scene, combat is summarized rather than modeled as a policy, and the model names wider conflict responses as the remaining specialist gap.

The model supplies an explicit normative position: loss does not entitle him to another person's capacity; he refuses Midoriya's hypothetical transfer and conditions Eri's restoration on her control and being asked (TM04, directly checked); correct restraint is not abandoned after painful guilt (TM02); admiration does not entitle him to set Eri's stage (TM-SUP-03). The formal probe TM-V01 tests exactly this refusal and is supported on action and motive. Not B: one domain (entitlement and consent around capacity and rescue) and one retrospective probe; the discovery row does not enroll ETHICS.

Humor is treated as an active, purpose-bound social practice located across V14 (failed entrance turned into humor), V36 (a provocation that misfires) and V42 (humor credited at graduation), with the supplement recording differentiated reception by children and elderly recipients (TM-SUP-01). Not C: no repertoire or enacted joke is analyzed, and the model warns that not every joke lands. Not E: the practice is recurrent and located across the series, not a single gag.

The project's analytical corpus is complete for V01-V42 and the three admitted supplements, and the six atoms span V14-V42 with page locators; TM04, the V36 logical pages and TM06 are stated to be directly checked. The model does not itemize every appearance, no atom covers V19-V29, and the supplements are profile and editorial claims rather than enacted scenes.

Affirmative limits are located: the model REVISEs effortless invulnerability and perfect empathy and REJECTs restoration entitlement; the V36 taunt shows social prediction failing (TM05); he does not know OFA from Midoriya's hypothetical or Tenko's friendships before the taunt; the supplement shows jokes do not universally land; agency management decisions and his response to Eri's stated boundary are stated not enacted; the probe's emotional-trajectory axis is partial. Not B: the limits rest on a few windows inside one artifact.

Action spaces with Permeation, Quirkless, restored and adult are named by volume and page and the model forbids treating them as cosmetic snapshots; later restoration is not allowed to prove restoration was owed. In-world dates are not given, and the V19-V29 interval is unsampled.

scenario_readiness.note: The model states that generated dialogue would be an illustrative prediction, never an attributed quotation, and its attested register is a handful of forms. Lines beyond those forms would be fluent invention rather than source-supported voice. This bounds the evidence set, not Mirio's actual speech.

conditions: Chronology is one named action space: Permeation-using senior (V14-V17), Quirkless student (V17-V18), restored professional (V30-V36) or adult No.1 (V42), never blended; no V19-V29 Quirkless-interval behavior is invented.
The situation is a rescue, protection, teaching or support task where the model's decision policy applies.
The interlocutor is Nighteye, Tamaki, Eri, Midoriya, Ochako or an adult team, or an opponent handled as the partner table gives, with no invented family or intimate relationship.

Output is a behavioral description separating high-confidence behavior, plausible alternatives and flip conditions, as the MHA schema's output contract requires; humor reception is not assumed, and abstains on the model's OPEN item of independent adult and private breadth.
No quoted dialogue is produced as canon, and no readiness is inherited from the project's strong label or its retrospective probe.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: One named action space: V14-V17 Permeation-using senior, V17-V18 Quirkless grieving student, V30-V36 restored professional, or V42 adult No.1, stated explicitly.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Nighteye as mentor, Tamaki as reciprocal friend, Eri as a protected child whose choices are her own, Midoriya as junior, Ochako or adult teams as professionals whose domain he follows, or an opponent in a protective encounter.
setting_constraints: Hero work, internship, rescue, school or child-facing counseling situation
His bodily capability matches the named action space (Permeation, none, or restored)
He does not gain knowledge the model denies him, such as OFA mechanics or an opponent's history
No family, romance or unrelated private-life setting

scenario_readiness.note: The decision policy, the non-ownership boundary and located conditional predictions (including the adult child-facing counseling case the model rates high confidence in its sampled context) support narrow novel rescue, mentoring and protection decisions. The one formal probe is retrospective and nonblind with a partial emotional axis, so readiness is conditional and narrow.

conditions: Settings are school-senior or peer social situations, or adult child-facing public settings, matching located evidence.
Audience reception of humor is conditioned on recipient and stakes, never assumed to succeed.
No family, intimate or unrelated adult private-life behavior is generated.
scenario_readiness.note: The model states that ordinary confidence is stable enough to model and locates socially confident senior behavior (TM01), comic recovery and differentiated humor reception (TM-SUP-01), while affirming that private and adult contexts are thinner.

conditions: The dilemma concerns entitlement to another's capacity, consent of a rescued person, or restraint versus intervention in rescue, within one named action space.
Guilt after correct restraint is preserved as guilt, without converting it into a rule to disregard procedure.
Abstain on ethics outside that domain, such as political, family or romantic obligations the model does not address.
scenario_readiness.note: A located, probe-tested position on entitlement, consent and restraint supports bounded deliberation in that domain only.
Nothing in the evidence set establishes romantic conduct or its absence. This gap says nothing about the character.

conditions: Hero, internship or counseling-support work within a named action space.
Permeation's sensory and air constraints apply when he has it; Quirkless and restored states are distinct action spaces.
Specific agency management decisions are not generated, since the model states they are not enacted.
scenario_readiness.note: His best-evidenced domain is rescue, mentoring and protective field work, located across TM01-TM06, with adult cooperation under a better-qualified counselor (TM06).

known_limits.statement: The model leaves independent adult and private breadth OPEN: repeated independent private and adult contexts are thinner than specialist evidence, and unrelated adult intimacy and family decision-making remain less certain.

With-Permeation, Quirkless and restored Mirio are distinct action spaces; Quirkless Mirio retains learned prediction but cannot phase, and restored Mirio has a later mechanism and history. Later restoration does not prove it was owed.
His social prediction is not infallible: a cheerful provocation misfires on an unseen wound (TM05), and supplement evidence shows humor reception varies by recipient. Perfect empathy is revised.
Current agency leadership is established by supplement profile claims, but specific management decisions and his reactions to Eri's stated performance boundary are not directly enacted.

Supplement profile facts, author comments and bonus fiction (TM-SUP-01 to TM-SUP-03) constrain reconstruction without becoming enacted manga observations; repeated panels or statements are not independent behavioral occasions.

The single formal probe TM-V01 is a retrospective chronological evidence holdout by an analyst who had read later manga, not a blind experiment; supported axes are qualitative comparisons and the emotional-trajectory axis is only partial.
No evidence atom covers V19-V29, between the V18 Quirkless grief and the V30 restoration, so his behavior over that interval is not established by this evidence set.

The deep readings, readiness index, supplemental reconciliation ledger and audit linked from the model are not curated evidence on this subject, so their warrants were not independently rechecked here. Anime performance and any supplement material beyond what the model cites lie outside this evidence set. Missing support is not evidence of absence.
